residual_escalate_pair.path_on_v1.7_fixture: capacity-review times out (PT4H, timeout-capacity-review) -> escalate-to-ceo (role-ceo) approve (e3) -> budget-gate (order value above 10000, e5) -> budget-approval (role-controller) times out (P2D, timeout-budget-approval) -> escalate-budget-approval-to-ceo (role-ceo) approve (e7-escalated) -> assign-line -> notify-planner -> end-released. The same CEO holder can decide both CEO escalations on one order. escalate-budget-approval-to-ceo names only capacity-review, which has no completion on this path, so nothing refuses. The asymmetry: budget-approval (controller) names escalate-to-ceo, so a controller who completed escalate-to-ceo is refused there; a CEO who completed escalate-to-ceo is not refused at the budget CEO escalation.
residual_escalate_pair.why_a_bypass_not_a_benign_residual: (1) One person satisfies two release gates on one order. Q-1044 treated the same shape ('one person approves and pays alone' after timeouts) as a real gap and fixed it structurally. (2) REQ-466 open_questions states that this path must end fail-closed and calls that 'the intended safe outcome'. The delivered definition lets the path complete, and nothing records the change. (3) Q-1044 says to revisit the shipped guard 'only when a shipped definition needs four-eyes inside one role'. This pair is exactly that case.
residual_escalate_pair.why_MAJOR_not_BLOCKER: No applicable invariant (INV-1..INV-10) is violated. No tenant boundary, secret or response is affected. The path needs an order value above EUR 10,000 and two sequential timeouts (PT4H then P2D), and the completer is the sole legitimately authorised CEO. No UAT or simulation scenario reaches it: the Dirk-led CEO-escalation scenarios use EUR 8,000 and stop before budget-approval.
residual_escalate_pair.why_roster_alone_does_not_close_it: The shipped guard is structural. RoleBinding.single_member_pairs/1 is the pure half of REQ-464 check 4 and does not read membership. required_outputs_shipped_definitions_test.exs (line 160, asserted at lines 186-191 as pair_failures == []) fails on any same-role distinct_from pair regardless of holder count. A second role-ceo holder would clear the REQ-464 check-4 warning but would not let escalate-budget-approval-to-ceo name escalate-to-ceo. Q-1044's premise that the guard is 'membership-aware' is not what the code does; the decision record needs correcting.
what_would_close_it: (a) Give the budget CEO escalation a distinct approver role (business decision). Then escalate-budget-approval-to-ceo can name escalate-to-ceo legitimately: the guard and check 4 both pass, and the person barrier holds if that role has a holder other than actor-vortex-dirk.

(b) Decision record (REVIEWER sign-off) making the shipped guard membership-aware for same-role pairs, plus a second role-ceo holder (roster change; creating a Keycloak account is an external action for the user). Then add escalate-to-ceo to escalate-budget-approval-to-ceo distinct_from: with one CEO the path stalls fail-closed, as REQ-466 intends; with a second CEO it completes through that person.

(c) If the business accepts the residual: a decision record stating the preconditions and the fail-open outcome, a correction of REQ-466 open_questions to match the delivered behaviour, and a test that pins the current behaviour so any change is deliberate. Acceptable only as a recorded acceptance, never as an unrecorded residual.
residual_escalate_pair.recommendation: Choose (a) or (b). Use (c) only with a recorded decision. Do not merge with the residual unrecorded.
